title: Sheaf kernel normalization of the supplied integral recollement maps
statement: Fix a six-functor operation datum [def-fix-six-functor-datum] on finite-type schemes over the geometric field. Let i:Z→X be a closed immersion and j:U→X the complementary open immersion, with X separated. Form the presentation whose open and closed functors are the datum's pull j followed by openExtension j and pull i followed by direct i, with the datum's actual counit and unit. This presentation satisfies SfIntegralRecollementNormalization [def-sf-recollement-presentation-data]: its two included outer functors are naturally isomorphic to the exact completed sheaf kernel and closed composite, and on every representative complex these isomorphisms identify its counit and unit with the localized kernel inclusion and closed sheaf unit, with the standard exact-functor factorizations. No triangle, connecting morphism, uniqueness, or Hom-vanishing assertion is included; empty strata are allowed.

source.place: Clause (3), source recollement; integral-stage adjunction and sheaf-sequence normalization in prop-sf-open-closed-triangle-all-stages.proof.md; Stacks 09AH and 015F.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-integral-support-functor-normalization] and [lem-sf-integral-immersion-pullback-normalization]. The latter supplies the ordinary/completed immersion comparisons on complete constructible inputs. The datum pullback equality and openRealization identify the supplied functors with these ordinary models. Use the actual completed direct-image realization on the closed side. These are natural comparisons of functors, not objectwise choices.

Restrict the ordinary open and closed adjunctions along the full constructible inclusions using [lem-sp-fully-faithful-adjunction-restriction]. Transfer the supplied adjunctions by uniqueness of left adjoints on the open side and right adjoints on the closed side. The unit and counit formulas carry the supplied maps to the ordinary maps; an arbitrary comparison of the underlying functors alone would not suffice.

The exact ringed open/closed sequence [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] identifies the ordinary open composite, with its counit, with the kernel and kernel inclusion of the closed unit. Coefficient transport and uniqueness of adjoints retain this description for the completed coefficient sheaves.

Localize the exact module adjunctions termwise using [def-weil-exact-derived-adjunction]. Their standard derived factorizations give the two natural outer isomorphisms. On Q(B), localization of the module counit and unit gives exactly the two equations of [def-sf-recollement-presentation-data]. Fullness restricts these identifications. Empty strata and zero inputs require no separate argument.

lean.statement:
theorem sfPackageIntegralRecollementNormalization
    {D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}} {C : D.CoefficientDatum}
    {E : Type u} [Field E] [Algebra (Padic C.l) E]
    [FiniteDimensional (Padic C.l) E] {n : ℕ} {hn : 1 ≤ n}
    (S : SixFunctorOperationDatum D C E n hn)
    {Z U X : SixFunctorSpace D} [IsSeparated X.obj.hom]
    (i : Z ⟶ X) (j : U ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i.hom.left]
    (hj : IsOpenImmersion j.hom.left)
    (hij : Set.range j.hom.left.base = (Set.range i.hom.left.base)ᶜ) :
    letI : LocallyOfFiniteType X.obj.hom := X.property.1
    letI : QuasiCompact X.obj.hom := X.property.2
    let P : SfRecollementPresentation (sfIntegralConstructibleCategory C.l E X.obj.left) :=
      ⟨S.higher.integral.pull j ⋙ S.higher.integral.openExtension j hj,
        S.higher.integral.pull i ⋙ S.higher.integral.direct i,
        (S.higher.integral.openAdjunction j hj).counit,
        (S.higher.integral.pullDirectAdjunction i).unit⟩
    SfIntegralRecollementNormalization C.l E i.hom.left
      (sfRecollementNoetherian D.k X.obj.left) P
